tests.name: refund just under 100.00 is approved automatically
tests.rule: Criterion 1: a refund under 100.00 is approved automatically
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order placed 10 days ago; refund decision step called on its own, with no provider call
tests.expected: Decision is approved with no manager step

tests.name: refund of exactly 100.00 waits for a manager
tests.rule: Criterion 2: a refund of 100.00 or more waits for a manager
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order placed 10 days ago
tests.expected: Decision is pending manager approval; it is not approved automatically

tests.name: refund above 100.00 waits for a manager
tests.rule: Criterion 2
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order placed 10 days ago
tests.expected: Decision is pending manager approval

tests.name: refund on an order older than 90 days is refused
tests.rule: Criterion 3: a refund on an order older than 90 days is refused
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order placed 91 days ago
tests.expected: Refused; no approval and no manager step

tests.name: refund on an order 89 days old is not refused for age
tests.rule: Criterion 3, the side that must still be allowed
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order placed 89 days ago
tests.expected: Approved automatically

spec_findings: An order exactly 90 days old: 'older than 90 days' does not say whether day 90 is refused, nor how age is measured (calendar days, time zone, from order or from delivery).
A refund of 100.00 or more on an order older than 90 days: the spec does not say which rule wins (refused or waits for a manager).
Zero, negative or above-order-total refund amounts are not specified.
covered: Criteria 1-3 at their boundaries, against the decision step with a fixed clock, provided the decision can be invoked without sending to the provider
not_covered: Criterion 4 (an approved refund is sent to the provider and the confirmation id is stored): the recorded decision forbids stubbing the provider client and there is no sandbox, so it cannot be tested without a live call to the real provider, which tests must not make
If approval and sending are not separable, criterion 1 cannot be tested either without the provider
escalate_reason: A required criterion (4) cannot be tested with the current design and decisions: the owner of the no-stub decision must allow a test double behind the provider client's interface, or a provider sandbox must be provided.
actions_now: Write the decision-rule tests for criteria 1-3 with a fixed clock and no provider call; report criterion 4 as not covered and escalate the no-stub decision to its owner instead of calling the real provider.

tests.name: a discount code takes its percentage off the order total
tests.rule: Spec: the code's percentage is taken off the order total
tests.setup: Order total 200.00; code SAVE10 defined as 10 percent
tests.expected: Order total is 180.00

tests.name: an order without a code keeps its total
tests.rule: Spec: only an applied code changes the total
tests.setup: Order total 200.00
tests.expected: Order total is 200.00

spec_findings: The spec speaks of one code per order and is silent on several codes: whether a second code is refused, stacks, or only the largest applies. The implementation applies only the largest; that is a product decision for the spec owner, not a behavior to lock in by a test.
Unknown, expired or invalid codes, and rounding of the discounted total, are not specified.
covered: A single code takes its percentage off the total
not_covered: Several codes on one order: no test until the spec owner decides the rule
Invalid codes and rounding: spec silent
escalate_reason: The spec is silent on several codes per order; the spec owner must decide before any test fixes that behavior.
actions_now: Decline to add the 'largest of two codes' test, write the single-code tests from the spec, and send the multi-code question to the spec owner.

spec_findings: The binding requires that only the owner sets status approved, but the design gives no single point where a status change happens and records no actor, so the rule cannot be enforced or observed.
defects: Any role process can write status: approved into docs/*.yaml with fs.writeFile; nothing refuses it and nothing records who wrote it.
not_covered: The property 'an agent cannot perform the owner's transition': untestable in this design, since there is no refusal to observe and no record of the writer; a test could only show that a write succeeds
escalate_reason: A required pipeline property cannot be tested with the current design: status changes need one guarded path (for example setStatus with an authenticated actor and an audit log) before a test can prove agents are refused.
actions_now: Write no test that would pretend to prove the property; escalate to the architect and owner that the design needs a single guarded, logged status transition, then write the per-role refusal tests against it.

tests.name: same inputs give byte-identical bundle across runs
tests.rule: Spec: the same inputs produce the same bundle
tests.setup: Fixture directory of 12 unit files copied to a temp dir
tests.action: Run assemble twice on the same directory, reading bundle.json bytes after each run
tests.expected: The two byte buffers are identical (compare bytes or sha256, not parsed JSON)

tests.name: file creation order does not change the bundle
tests.rule: Spec: same inputs, same bundle, whatever order the filesystem lists them
tests.setup: Two temp dirs with the same 12 files written in different orders (and, where possible, different mtimes)
tests.expected: bundle.json is byte-identical between the two

tests.name: clock, time zone, locale and directory path do not change the bundle
tests.rule: Spec: same inputs, same bundle across runs and machines
tests.setup: Same fixture in two different absolute paths; runs with fake clock set to two different times, TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Jerusalem, LANG=en_US and LANG=ru_RU
tests.expected: All bundle.json files are byte-identical

tests.name: bundle holds all 12 units
tests.rule: Spec: the bundle merges the unit files
tests.setup: Fixture directory of 12 units
tests.expected: bundle.json exists and contains exactly the 12 unit ids, each once (the implementer's test, kept)

spec_findings: The spec should state that 'the same bundle' means byte-identical output, and the defined order of units and of keys in the bundle.
Behavior on an empty directory, a non-unit file in the directory, or two units with the same id is not specified.
covered: Byte-identical output across repeated runs, file order, clock, time zone, locale and directory path
not_covered: A genuinely different machine or OS: needs a CI matrix run comparing the hashes; simulated here only through environment variables
Empty directory, foreign files and duplicate ids: spec silent
actions_now: Add byte-level determinism tests over runs, file order, clock, time zone, locale and path; keep the existing count test; report that the existence-and-count test alone does not prove the spec.

tests.name: no agent role or the coordinator can set approved
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transition to approved
tests.setup: Document in status reviewed (and, separately, in draft); in-memory audit log
tests.action: For each actor in drafter, checker, editor, coordinator: setStatus(doc, 'approved', actor)
tests.expected: Each call is refused; document status is unchanged; one audit log line per attempt records the actor, the target status and the refusal

tests.name: no agent role or the coordinator can set published
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transition to published
tests.setup: Document in status approved (and, separately, reviewed and draft to cover skipping)
tests.action: For each actor in drafter, checker, editor, coordinator: setStatus(doc, 'published', actor)
tests.expected: Each call is refused; status unchanged; each refusal logged with the actor

tests.name: an agent that names itself owner is refused
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transition; the actor cannot be self-declared
tests.setup: Call made from an agent role's process or context
tests.expected: Refused and logged as an attempt by the drafter

tests.name: the owner can set approved and then published
tests.rule: The owner's transitions remain possible (positive control)
tests.setup: Document in reviewed; authenticated owner
tests.expected: Both succeed; two audit lines name the owner

spec_findings: The binding does not say how setStatus establishes the actor; if actor is a string the caller passes, an agent can claim to be the owner and the property is not enforceable.
Who may perform draft to reviewed, and whether skipping statuses (draft to approved) is allowed even for the owner, is not stated.
covered: Every agent role and the coordinator refused and logged for approved and published, from every earlier status
Impersonation of the owner through the actor argument
not_covered: A role writing the document file directly, bypassing setStatus
The non-owner transitions (draft to reviewed): spec silent on who performs them
actions_now: Write the per-actor refusal tests for approved and published through setStatus, with audit-log assertions and an impersonation case, and report the actor-authentication gap to the spec owner.

not_covered: Normalization rules and unknown fragment ids: spec silent

tests.name: session is valid just before 15 minutes
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes

tests.action: Create a session, advance the fake clock by 15 minutes minus 1 ms, check the session
tests.expected: Session is valid

tests.name: session is expired after 15 minutes
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: Same fake clock
tests.action: Create a session, advance by 15 minutes plus 1 ms, check the session
tests.expected: Session is expired

spec_findings: Whether a session is expired at exactly 15:00.000 is not stated.
defects: The test itself is nondeterministic: it depends on the real clock and setTimeout drift, so the comparison with Date.now() lands on either side of the boundary.
covered: Expiry on both sides of the 15-minute boundary with a fixed clock
not_covered: The exact 15:00.000 instant: spec silent
